searchText: simple one, shouldn't `value: Gwei` be `value: uint256` in the header? generally speaking, on CL interfaces it's Gwei where is this? The modified `ExecutionPayloadHeader`, I have just been comparing it to the builder bid in the builder-specs https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/blob/main/specs/bellatrix/builder.md#builderbid but actually `Gwei` (uint64) is more accurate, so can ignore this question. oh, yeah EPH would have Gwei it's firmly a CL creature If value is the value of the execution payload then it should be a `uint256`, as it could be (pretty much) any value of Wei. it is the value of the execution payload, ah yeah the `blockValue` from the engine api is wei, forgot about that would be I think the first `UInt256` in a CL layer proper if it's put in EPH. worth considering, since this ends up in `BeaconState` etc the engine/builder approach amounts to having a wrapper object with the block (or block + blobs, or bid, or etc) + the value It is the value of the bid, and it stays Gwei over my dead body I suspect you have your idiom the wrong way around. Are you trying to say that it should stay as a gwei value, and not be turned into a uint256? If so, will there not be issues when the gwei value is incorrect compared to reality? And if not, why is this value in state? This value is what is deducted from the builder in a payment to the proposer for including his block. There is no need for this value to be WEI since we can only deduct Gwei in the beaconchain anyway. This value **may be obtained** from comparison reasons, from the corresponding Wei value in the engine API from the local block, but that Wei value is useless for purposes of this beacon state entry. The reason this has to be in the state it is because the builder's payment is part of consensus we could always lift the API decision to the CL spec, and that's the part that I say "over my dead body", no way in hell this turns into a 32 byte unnecessary object as it is already unnecessary in the API So does the builder supply this value in gwei, or could it supply it in wei? it supplies it in gwei, that's the header that they are talking about, it's signed by the builder Oh yes of course, all BN operations are in Gwei. Forgot to convert the engine `value` from wei to gwei in the code, and failed the gossip builder's balance validation. That's why I brought it up here. Now it's clear. It seems like it's easier to unbundle in the same slot in ePBS slot auction than mev-boost today since PTC just votes for timeliness and the next slot proposer could simply choose to build on top of the "stolen-mev" block Don't want to raise PR again to close seconds after 😀 , but looking at the state upgrade and we have `latest_execution_payload_header=ExecutionPayloadHeader()`,we should set the block_hash from the `pre.latest_execution_payload_header` rather than "ZERO" it. Alternatively we could say that `is_parent_block_full` should always return true before `EIP7732_FORK_EPOCH` if we worry about edge cases yeah, fork.md sets the state.latest_block_hash to the same Ya this makes sense to me https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3924

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
I suspect you have your idiom the wrong way around.  Are you trying to say that it should stay as a gwei value, and not be turned into a uint256?

If so, will there not be issues when the gwei value is incorrect compared to reality?  And if not, why is this value in state?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: This value is what is deducted from the builder in a payment to the proposer for including his block. There is no need for this value to be WEI since we can only deduct Gwei in the beaconchain anyway. This value **may be obtained** from comparison reasons, from the corresponding Wei value in the engine API from the local block, but that Wei value is useless for purposes of this beacon state entry. The reason this has to be in the state it is because the builder's payment is part of consensus

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: we could always lift the API decision to the CL spec, and that's the part that I say "over my dead body", no way in hell this turns into a 32 byte unnecessary object as it is already unnecessary in the API

excerpts.content: So does the builder supply this value in gwei, or could it supply it in wei?
